text:
Owen Park: hey folks, first morning! set up Homebrew + asdf on my M1 MBA but VS Code launched from the dock isn't picking up asdf shims, so editor terminals use system python/node. any recommended fix? :wave:
DevX Bot: welcome Owen! common cause is GUI apps not inheriting shell rc. paste `which python`, `echo $SHELL`, and your shell rc file (`~/.zprofile` vs `~/.zshrc`) entries.
Owen Park: which python -> /Users/owen/.asdf/shims/python, echo $SHELL -> /bin/zsh, but ~/.zshrc only has aliases, i put PATH edits in ~/.zprofile as per dotfiles. Editor still shows /usr/bin/python.
Leila: macOS only sources login shells for apps launched from Finder/dock. Put PATH and asdf init into ~/.zprofile (login) or use the launchctl approach. Example in ~/.zprofile:
```
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH"
. $(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh
```
Marco: if you don't want to restart, run `launchctl setenv PATH "$(echo $PATH)"` then reopen VS Code. That injects env into GUI processes. Another option: always launch code from terminal with `code .` to inherit shell env.
Owen Park: tried moving lines to ~/.zprofile and did `launchctl setenv PATH \"$PATH\"` then restarted VS Code. Terminal now picks up asdf shims, but Python extension still points to a different interpreter.
Sophie: VS Code stores a selected interpreter per-workspace. Open Command Palette -> Python: Select Interpreter and pick the one under ~/.asdf/shims (should show the correct 3.11). Also check devcontainer or remote workspace settings if present.
Owen Park: selected the asdf interpreter, good. quick follow-up: when installing node with asdf it failed building some native deps and suggested Rosetta. Any guidance?
Leila: for x86 native builds you can run the shell under Rosetta: duplicate Terminal in Applications -> Get Info -> Open using Rosetta, then install node there. But we prefer native arm builds. If a package needs node-gyp, install Xcode command line tools and `brew install python@3.11 pkg-config cairo libffi` etc. Often `npm rebuild` fixes.
Marco: also check .tool-versions in the repo root — we pin node/python versions there. run `asdf install` in the repo to install everything at once.
Owen Park: where do I find company dotfiles and the setup script? want git hooks and core.autocrlf set.
DevX Bot: dotfiles repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dotfiles. Run: `git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/dotfiles ~/dotfiles && cd ~/dotfiles && ./setup.sh`. It symlinks and installs pre-commit hooks.
Sophie: note the setup will prompt to import 1password sessions for direnv. If you use 1password.app, run `eval $(op signin --raw your)` in a terminal before running the setup so direnv can load secrets. We also have a helper `scripts/bootstrap.sh` in the dotfiles that checks prerequisites.
Owen Park: ran setup, direnv denied because OP_SESSION missing. signed into 1password CLI, allowed direnv, hooks installed. all green. thanks! :tada:
Leila: welcome aboard! ping me if you want me to walk through VS Code launch nuances or if any native build errors persist.
Owen Park: appreciate it, tagging @Leila if anything else pops up.
